title: Can you help me learn to enjoy the movies of Richard Linklater? I've tried to watch Dazed and Confused, for instance, several times but keep getting bored.

commenti.body: [removed]

If you stopped watching after fifteen minutes because it was that boring, genuinely I think the movie is just not for you.

Everyone is going to have their own tastes and experiences with different films and the way they portray their characters, events, and themes. This one I don't think any level of rationalisation is going to make you enjoy, and it's a waste of time to think that just because it is popular you necessarily need to like it.

Linklater movies are very natural and held back.

If Slice of Life isn't for you maybe you can't be a fan.

You probably won't like Boyhood either.

Maybe give the "Before" trilogy a try. I think they have the most engaging dialogue.

Dazed is my favorite movie. To start with, what you said about the movie not working towards a goal is mostly true and it’s one of the best things about it to me. This is a high school movie. Following the lives of high schoolers. So the stakes of this movie is only a piece of paper to sign for the football team but to a high schooler, that would be the biggest deal in the world. Every interaction in that movie I can think of someone I knew like that or a situation I was in like it. It’s not a plot driven movie. It’s a movie you can kick back and enjoy the ride and, if you let yourself, feel nostalgic for those times in your own life. I was born in the 90’s and have never lived in Texas so I should have zero relation to this movie. But the fact is that these kinds of social interactions are timeless

A lot of his films are what is called "slice of life." Nothing crazy happens, sometimes very little or no plot, it's more of a window into these characters lives for a period of time. They are one of my favorite genres as they feel very natural and real. If you're used to more structured storytelling then it may take some getting used to. To be a bit silly here it's kinda like vibes based. You walk around in a characters shoes for a while just to see what their life is like, that's the point, the point isn't some adventure or conflict.

I would keep trying new ones, because it really may just be that you aren't used to this kind of story and you've gotta build up an appreciation of it. And it really is a fantastic genre containing many wonderful films. But if any one movie isn't hitting you don't need to don't suffer through it, just turn it off and try a different one another time.

Linklater's filmography is all over the place.  He's made enough different kinds of movies that there's probably something in there for you.  My personal favorites are Slacker and Before Sunset.  They're not very similar.

My 2 cents: if you want to “get” Linklater, start with some of his commercial/director for hire projects and then try one of his more autuer-projects. 

I think the double-triple-quad feature might be: 

School of Rock - leans more to the Jack Black show but gives you restrained Linklater. You see how he makes HIS commercial “slacker-vs-snobs” movie. 

Slacker or boyhood depending on your age - to me, slacker is the uncut Linklater. He’s 100% still figuring it out but it’s a great experiment. Same for Boyhood- it’s an experiment that doesn’t 100% work for some but as someone closer to the protagonists’ age, the meandering ebbs/flows really hooked me. 

Bad News Bears - “Hired gun Linklater” strikes again, but this time it’s the Billy Bob show. Doesn’t 100% work but gives you the narrative structure to latch onto. 

“Before” movies - a lot of people’s favorites. Emblematic of the slice of life he’s known for. 

Or none of these, one or none of them might strike your fancy. But no shame in that

If you don't want to listen to someone's conversation on a bus then you likely won't appreciate other Linklater flicks. Especially the Before trilogy which arguably hangs on the premise of the two people in conversation on a train falling in love.

A more recent entry in the 'slice of life's category that I really appreciated was Apollo 10 1/2. It's animated and the gaps in period locales/props are expertly filled in, also Jack Black's narration is 🤌🏼. It feels like running through the sprinkler as a kid.

Special mention to a couple of his more recent directorial outings, Bernie and Last Flag Flying. They aren't overtly Libklatery. Both have actual plots.

As others have stated, "Dazed" is a type of "slice of life" film, though more specifically it's a coming of age film. The only goal for the characters is to find their own way in life, despite what the adults say.

Coming of age films, by my estimation, have to be either relatable to you. When I was a stoner teenager, I loved this movie because I saw myself in the characters. As an adult, I just think it's ok. 

By the same token, I enjoyed "Dead Poets Society" as a kid, but as an adult I found it underwhelming. My wife, on the other hand, couldn't get into it at all, partly because she's no longer a teenager, and partly because there are no real female characters (takes place at a boys boarding school...)

To answer your question, I'd recommend "School of Rock", which is more traditionally structured and is more about accepting your own limitations as an adult. If you're a fan of Phillip K. Dick's books, "A Scanner Darkly" is the most faithful adaptation IMHO

Do you generally like movies that are true to life or do you need car crashes and explosions? The movies you watched aren’t “documentaries,” they are just dramas. You might give *Slacker* a shot. It’s the movie that made him famous and is weird and funny. You might not like it if you have issues with micro-budget filmmaking. *School of Rock* is his best commercial movie. If you haven’t seen it, definitely give it a go. *Bernie* is a weird little black comedy. *Waking Life* and *A Scanner Darkly* are rotoscoped animations. *Before Sunrise* is a lovely romance. If you like it then you have two sequels to watch.

Linklater has a unique brand of humanist filmmaking that I'm sure some people just won't enjoy. His early breakout was Slacker, which is kind of a pop-philsophical, stream of consciousness dialogue-driven movie. He later reprised this idea with Waking Life, which took it up a notch and used the rotoscoping animation technique that he later used in A Scanner Darkly and Apollo 10 1/2.

Probably his most celebrated movies are the Before Sunrise trilogy. I'd recommend Before Sunrise, as a better example of Linklater over Dazed.

Its important to keep in mind that Dazed is minor work of his. It just happens to be a crowd favorite, for whatever reason. I don't dislike it, but its one of my least favorite Linklater movies. I'd put it somewhere between Fast Food Nation and Bernie. It lacks the heart and character of his movies and really doesn't even feel like a Linklater movie. There's nothing in the story, dialogue or characters that resonates with me. If I'm being honest, its kind of basic and dumb when you compare it to his great movies.

I really don't think there is much to "get" with Dazed and Confused. I think it's a hilarious movie because I was a huge pothead as a teenager and in my early 20's, and that movie does an excellent job of poking fun at and playing with the personality types that I associated with during those years. In that sense, it absolutely felt like a documentary that showed an evening of my later highschool years. I really can't say I would find it entertaining or compelling if I didn't connect with that time or if the characters didn't all remind me of friends of mine.
School of Rock is one of the best comedies this century imo, it’s so fucking heartwarming without being too cheesy

I think he’s one of those directors. If the “hang out” style of movie where dialogue and interpersonal interaction dominate the screen do not appeal to you, I don’t think his movies would be for you. But that’s totally fine, everyone has those directors that just don’t work for them. I personally love him though, his movies just make me feel so (this is going to sound corny as hell) warm.

his films are not documentary, it is more like slice of life. to enjoy Linklater's films, you have to be able to love and appreciate the mundanity of life. You need to be able to perceive the minutia of life as cinematic and worthy of reliving on the screen. If you need lights, spectacle, or stimuli to be intrigued by what's happening on the screen, then you are not going to connect with a lot of Linklater's films, especially stuff like Dazed & Confused of the Before trilogy. It also comes down to a philosophical sense of what cinema means to you and what you look for or expect to see in a film. Is film purely meant for spectacle? or can it be a medium that depicts and reveal the human experience?

Everything you dislike about Linklater is the reason I love him. No melodrama often there’s very little conflict even. He doesn’t show, he tells. Just like real people do. His films feel so real. Watching Boyhood I feel like a genuine fly on the wall. I know that’s a cliche expression but Linklater (along with Cassavetes) truly make me feel that way.
